business_scope.primary_industry_name: Trailing Suction Hopper Dredging and Rubble Mound Breakwater Works

stage_1.document_name: Certified copy of passport (and residence proof) of each UBO/shareholder
stage_1.issuing_entity: Notary or competent authority in country of origin
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) OR consular legalization by French Embassy/Consulate for non-Hague countries

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (SARL); general company provisions L.210-1 to L.210-10; register formalities under L.123-1 to L.123-17 and R.123-101 et seq.; Guichet Unique teleprocedure per Law PACTE 2019-486.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) via the INPI Guichet Unique portal at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form M0 (Déclaration de création d'une société) filed electronically with the French Articles of Association (Statuts) executed either under private signature (sous seing privé) or notarially if real property is contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; the statutes may fix the share capital at EUR 1 (Article L.223-2). However, 100% of the subscribed cash capital must be fully paid up at incorporation and deposited within eight days of receipt into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) at a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the funds are released only upon presentation of the RCS Kbis extract. In-kind contributions of vessels or machinery require appraisal by a commissaire aux apports.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF [COMPANY] SARL. Under Articles L.223-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code, the undersigned shareholders, having fully subscribed the entire capital, resolve: (1) to adopt the annexed draft Articles of Association; (2) to certify the capital fully paid up under applicable escrow rules; (3) to establish the registered office at [Registered Address], France; (4) to appoint [Full Name] as sole Gérant, with full powers to bind the company and complete all statutory, tax and social formalities; and (5) to authorize the corporate service provider to file the dossier with the INPI Guichet Unique, publish the legal notice and obtain RCS registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Signature of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders acting under private signature; notaire public required where real estate or a vessel under mortgage is contributed to the company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SARL statutes in French containing corporate name, legal form, registered office, corporate purpose (maritime dredging and public maritime works), share capital, duration of 99 years, class of shares, management powers of the Gérant, audit and approval thresholds, and dispute resolution clauses; obtain unanimous consent of all founding shareholders; initial each page and execute the final signature block. If in-kind contributions exceeding approximately EUR 30,000 or special advantages are made, appoint a commissaire aux apports to file an appraisal report.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each founding shareholder
Draft Articles of Association (Statuts)
Contribution agreements and valuation report of commissaire aux apports (if in-kind)
Proof of corporate name availability (INPI trademark or RCS negative certificate)
Power of attorney for each shareholder represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS registrar later objects to any statutory clause, amend the clause by an extraordinary shareholders' decision and file a rectified act at the registry; do not submit the formation dossier before the statutes fully comply with Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Full Payment and Escrow Blocking of the Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the bank issues the statutory deposit certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the 'société en formation'; transfer the total subscribed cash capital from the shareholders' own bank accounts; obtain the 'certificat du dépositaire des fonds' evidencing full payment; the funds remain frozen until the Gérant produces the RCS registration extract (Kbis), after which the bank releases the balance.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC and AML identification files for every shareholder
Beneficial owner declaration (UBO) of each subscribing entity
Pro-forma Articles of Association approved by the bank
Share transfer or debit advices proving the capital movements
Bank account opening application and signatory mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit for insufficient KYC evidence, complete the beneficial-ownership and source-of-funds declarations and re-submit; alternatively block the funds at the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations. Comply with the strict eight-day deposit window of Article L.223-7 of the Commercial Code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Statutory Incorporation Notice in a Legal Announcement Gazette (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A certified Journal d'Annonces Légales authorized in the department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and publish a French-language notice stating the corporate name followed by 'SARL', the registered office address, corporate purpose, share capital, duration, the full names of the Gérant, and the RCS city of filing; obtain the 'attestation de parution' proving publication; the notice must be inserted within 30 days following signature of the statutes.
required_dossiers: Final signed Articles of Association
Approved wording of the legal notice (vetted by counsel)
Order form and publication fee receipt of the JAL
Identity documents of shareholders and manager for the publication file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL's editorial board refuses the notice for non-compliance with Article R.210-5 of the Commercial Code, reformulate the notice to include all mandatory legal items and republish in an alternate gazette; no reimbursement of the refused insertion fee applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Complete Incorporation Dossier with the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) - Guichet Unique portal at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Connect to the portal, select 'Création d'une société commerciale (SARL)', complete the M0 declaration, upload all mandatory documents in PDF, pay the official fees by bank card, and submit. Track the status online; a 'dossier complet' receipt triggers transmission to the RCS greffe, while a 'dossier incomplet' notice grants a statutory cure period for missing items.
required_dossiers: M0 company creation declaration completed online
Signed Articles of Association (unabridged PDF)
Certificat du dépositaire des fonds issued by the bank
Attestation de parution from the JAL
Domiciliation agreement or lease for the registered office
Passport or national ID of the appointed Gérant
Déclaration sur l'honneur de non-condamnation of the Gérant
Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs (RBO)
Payment receipt of official registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the INPI portal issues a notice of incompleteness, submit the missing pieces online within 15 calendar days; if the dossier is rejected, correct the deficiencies and re-file against a new fee payment. Where the activity is deemed regulated, provide the manager's professional qualification certificate or amend the corporate purpose before re-submission.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through impots.gouv.fr and the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). French business formation and registration filings are submitted through the INPI-operated Guichet unique; the resulting registration data are transmitted to the relevant authorities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is registered through the INPI Guichet unique and receives a SIREN and SIRET after registration in the Registre national des entreprises. The competent SIE assigns or confirms the French intracommunity VAT number, generally in the format FR plus a two-digit key and the SIREN. The company must activate its professional account on impots.gouv.fr for tax filings and payments. A foreign entity making taxable supplies in France without a French establishment applies to the DGFiP Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères for VAT registration before or upon commencing taxable transactions. There is generally no turnover threshold for a non-established taxable person. A non-EU/EEA-established applicant may need to appoint an accredited French fiscal representative, subject to applicable legal exceptions; an EU-established applicant generally does not.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Eligible SARLs may elect temporary partnership taxation under the conditions and time limits in the French Tax Code, generally for up to five fiscal years. A SARL formed by members of the same family may, if statutory conditions are met, elect partnership taxation without that five-year limit. A SARL may also elect the special partnership-tax treatment available to a qualifying SARL de famille. France does not have a US-style check-the-box regime. Classification and treaty treatment depend on French law and the entity's legal characteristics; hybrid mismatch rules may deny deductions or require income inclusion in specified cases.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold applies to a non-established taxable person making taxable supplies in France; VAT registration is generally required from the first taxable transaction. For eligible French-established small businesses, the domestic VAT exemption (franchise en base) is subject to statutory turnover thresholds and conditions, which vary by activity and applicable tax year; it does not generally exempt a non-established supplier from registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing for domestic B2B transactions between VAT-taxable persons established in France and electronic transaction reporting for specified transactions outside that invoicing scope. From 1 September 2026, all in-scope businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices; issuance obligations begin on that date for large and intermediate-sized businesses and on 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-businesses. In-scope invoices must use an approved platform or the public invoicing portal under the applicable rules and structured formats. France does not generally require real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping of every invoice. Cross-border transactions, consumer transactions, and other reportable operations may be subject to e-reporting rather than domestic e-invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the EU may be exempt from French VAT with a right to deduct input VAT when statutory conditions are met and the supplier can substantiate that the goods left the EU. Intra-EU supplies are subject to separate exemption rules, including customer VAT-number and transport-evidence requirements. Services are not automatically zero-rated as exports: place-of-supply rules determine whether French VAT applies, and specific exemptions may apply to qualifying services directly connected with exports or international transport. Marine dredging and seawall works require transaction-specific analysis, including the location of immovable-property-related services, customer status, and any applicable domestic reverse-charge rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration with the applicable export MRN and electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice and contract identifying the goods, customer, destination, and applicable VAT exemption basis
Bill of lading, sea waybill, or other carrier transport document, together with delivery and transport records
Customer order, proof of payment, and accounting records reconciling the transaction and export proceeds
For services, contract, work records, location evidence, customer VAT-status evidence where relevant, and documentation supporting the applicable place-of-supply or exemption rule
An inward remittance certificate is not a general French VAT zero-rating requirement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France imposes no general statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Export exemption depends on satisfying the applicable legal conditions and retaining reliable evidence. Unsupported or incorrectly exempted supplies may be assessed for VAT, late-payment interest, and tax penalties; intentional or fraudulent conduct can attract aggravated penalties and, where applicable, criminal sanctions. Input VAT refunds may be denied or recovered, and assessments may generally be reopened within the applicable statutory limitation period, subject to extensions or exceptions for fraud and other specified circumstances.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in its capacity as the Eurosystem national central bank, with foreign-exchange policy and balance-of-payments reporting functions exercised under the French Monetary and Financial Code. The Direction Générale du Trésor exercises State Treasury oversight, while the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) supervises credit institutions and anti-money-laundering obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a Eurozone member with fully liberalised capital and current-account convertibility under Articles 63 to 66 TFEU, Directive 88/361/EEC and the French Monetary and Financial Code. The euro is freely convertible into other currencies without exchange-control approval. Current-account payments covering trade invoices, subcontractor fees, interest, royalties and profit distributions can be settled without a French foreign-exchange licence. Profit remittance hurdles are indirect rather than prohibitive: the French SARL must demonstrate real business substance, maintain audited accounts, meet withholding tax and tax-treaty requirements on distributions to non-resident shareholders, and ensure no EU/CFSP sanctions screening failure arises. The receiving French bank is required to report reportable cross-border transactions to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics, but this is a declaratory regime, not a convertibility restriction. For capital-account operations such as shareholder capital increases, subordinated loans and equity repatriation, no prior exchange-control authorisation exists; the transaction must be documented with corporate resolutions, financing agreements and a lawful economic purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: French law imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender, no statutory remittance timeline and no conversion ratio. A French exporter may retain foreign-currency receivables in a foreign-currency account, convert them to euro, or use them for permitted treasury settlement. The only legal obligations are the balance-of-payments declaration submitted by the resident bank to Banque de France for reportable transactions, and the exporter's obligation to maintain commercial documentation sufficient to identify the export, the counterparty and the payment flow. No drachma-era or euro-era surrender rule remains in force. In practice, for clean audit and banking compliance, export proceeds should be credited within normal agreed trade terms, evidenced by customs declarations, invoices, and settlement advice.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational euro current account, multi-currency account, capital escrow account (compte sequestre)
Operational current account, trade finance account, project disbursement account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate treasury clearing account, SWIFT asset-liquidity account, FX hedging account
Trade finance and letter-of-credit account, project escrow account for marine infrastructure milestones

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury banking rail and capital escrow provider; Medium as an ancillary payment-processing rail. Legal constraints are definitive under French law: an offshore digital EMI that is not established or passported into France under Directive 2009/110/EC and the PSD2 framework cannot lawfully hold funds, open a treasury account or settle cross-border payments for a French SARL. Any payment institution, electronic money institution or crypto-asset service provider must be licensed or passported into the French market and registered with the ACPR and/or ORIAS. Even an EEA-licensed EMI may only provide payment services and cannot provide deposit accounts, credit facilities, FX treasury limits or commercial cash escrow as a substitute for a licensed credit institution. Therefore, the SARL should use an EMI only as a supplemental disbursement rail for low-value operational payments, never as the treasury account holder for capital or port-authority milestone funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML/KYC regulation requires the legal representative, the gérant/directors and ultimate beneficial owners to be identified and verified before account opening. In tier-1 commercial banks, at least one authorised signatory is expected to attend an in-person interview at a French branch; remote video identification is legally permissible under ACPR-compliant procedures using certified identity verification, liveliness detection and documentary verification, but foreign-owned corporate structures without significant French operating history generally attract a mandatory physical interview for the principal shareholder and managing director. A French SARL with an offshore shareholder should budget for the physical presence of the manager and one shareholder representative during onboarding. The bank will require a copy of the statuts, the register of beneficial owners (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), proof of statutory publication, valid passports, one current bank reference, corporate organigramme and source-of-funds evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident natural person controls the SARL and is identified as the sole or majority ultimate beneficial owner without a clear lineage of accumulated wealth or prior banking relationship in France.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Personal and corporate KYC bundle: officially certified passport of the UBO, tax residence certificate from the home jurisdiction, notarised articles or corporate deed of the SARL, registered beneficial-ownership declaration filed with the French trade registry, two years of audited financial statements for the shareholder entity or personal accounts, source-of-wealth statement supported by asset acquisition contracts, inheritance documents, salary records, sale-and-purchase agreements and a bank reference from a licensed credit institution with at least 12 months of transactional history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company is engaged in marine dredging and maritime construction with counterparties or vessel charters involving states subject to EU restrictive measures, or the project refers to port facilities in embargoed or disputed territorial waters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance and project veracity file: tender or public procurement award notice, port authority concession or work order, flag and IMO registration certificates for all dredging vessels, export licences if any element involves dual-use items, customs classification proof, insurance policies covering political risk, sanctions and PEP screening reports for all parties and subcontracted vessel owners, and a written undertaking that no vessel will call at ports in sanctioned jurisdictions during the contract term.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection originated from a jurisdiction perceived as a money-laundering or offshore risk, is structured as a series of high-value payments, or lacks a clear taxable legal basis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital movement file: executed shareholder loan or capital increase agreement, board and extraordinary shareholder meeting minutes approving the inflow, notarised legalisation or apostille from the remitter's jurisdiction, bank-to-bank MT103 or ISD input showing complete remitter identification, proof of origin of funds such as audited accounts of the parent, corporate bank statements supporting the source of the transferred moneys, and a legal opinion confirming the transaction is not an artificial arrangement under French substance requirements or EU tax-disclosure (DAC6) rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to be made to independent subcontractors in EEA low-tax or non-registry jurisdictions without an established operational footprint, or subcontractors structurally identical to shell entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vendor due-diligence file: commercial quotation and signed subcontract, invoice with full bank account identifiers, proof of registration in the subcontractor's local trade register, VAT or equivalent registration number, evidence of physical office or staff, UBO attestation, professional and environmental licences for dredging works, evidence of insurance coverage for marine operations, sanctions screening report, and declaration that the vendor performs substantive works rather than acting as a pass-through intermediary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a capital increase or intercompany shareholder loan to a French SARL, the compliant routing is a SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR remittances or a SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments from within the EEA. The beneficiary must be the SARL itself, in the bank account titled to the SARL's French SIREN number. The payment text must include the exact corporate transaction reference, the upstream contract or resolution number, and a brief purpose, for example 'shareholder capital increase under French Company Law' or 'intercompany loan agreement dated [date]'. The French resident bank will ask for the underlying corporate deed and shareholder approval. For reportable amounts the bank will classify the operation under the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting scheme and may require a 'motif' code corresponding to capital transaction or financing operation. The receiving bank must also screen the transfer against EU and UN sanctions lists. No French exchange-control permit is required. For a contribution to share capital, the statutory corporate procedure must be completed before settlement is accepted; for a loan, a fully executed loan agreement, interest rate evidence and repayment schedule must be lodged with the bank file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements for marine dredging procurement, subcontract labour, equipment charters and port dues should be cleared on the following rails: SEPA Credit Transfer for direct EUR payments to beneficiaries inside the SEPA zone; SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA or non-EUR payments to international suppliers; documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 for the purchase of capital marine equipment or through suppliers requiring payment against documents; and standby letters of credit or dematerialised bank guarantees for performance bonds payable to the port authority or main contractor. For high-value EUR clearing inside the Eurosystem, TARGET2 or its successor T2 service provides immediate final settlement. Outbound payment instructions must carry the underlying contract number, invoice reference, the exact beneficiary bank BIC and IBAN where available, and a truthful payment purpose code consistent with the French balance-of-payments classifications. The bank will verify that each disbursement corresponds to a genuine construction or procurement milestone before authorisation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forward between euro and freely convertible counterpart currencies, such as EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF, concluded with an EU-authorised credit institution or investment firm under an ISDA/CSA or French master agreement.

Cross-currency interest rate swap denominated in EUR against USD or GBP, permissible where the SARL has a genuine underlying commercial exposure from the dredging contract, supplier obligations or port-authority milestone payments.
Vanilla FX option contract on EUR/USD or EUR/GBP purchased or structured under MiFID II with clear risk acknowledgement and eligible counterparty or professional classification for the SARL.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for currencies whose local settlement is administratively restricted or where a fully deliverable market is unavailable; permitted only where the underlying obligation is real and verifiable, and the counterparty is a licensed credit institution reporting the transaction under EMIR with post-trade margin arrangements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) and statutory audit report filed with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) / INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal-year end (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December year-end); extendable by court order for up to an additional 3 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil fine up to EUR 5,000 against the legal representative; court injunction under astreinte (daily penalty); continued non-filing may lead to judicial dissolution or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale, including form 2065-SD and schedules 2050-SD to 2059-SD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: second working day following 1 May (typically 3 May; if that day falls on a weekend or public holiday, the following business day)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; 10% late-filing penalty if unfiled within 30 days; 40% for bad-faith non-compliance; 80% for organised tax fraud.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registration data (déclaration annuelle de confirmation des mentions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fourth quarter of each calendar year (1 October through 31 December) for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Repeated failure to confirm may result in the removal of the company from the RCS, loss of legal personality, and inability to invoke registration against third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CVAE annual return and payment, plus CFE instalment/assessment (contribution économique territoriale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CVAE: second working day after 1 May for the preceding calendar year; CFE: tax notice issued mid-year, final payment due on 15 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% penalty for inaccurate or incomplete CVAE declaration; 10% for failure to file after formal notice; 0.20% monthly interest; CFE late payment subject to a 10% surcharge plus monthly interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO register update (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) following any share transfers or ownership changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; if bundled with the annual confirmation, any update must be filed by 31 December of the confirmation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 18,750 for a legal entity and EUR 3,750 for a natural person (Monetary and Financial Code, Art. L.574-5); criminal sanctions may apply for intentional concealment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory commissaire aux comptes appointment when a SARL exceeds two of three thresholds at fiscal year-end: total balance sheet > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees > 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (PCG – ANC Regulation 2014-03); IFRS as adopted by the EU is mandatory for consolidated public-interest groups and optional at the consolidated level for non-listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial-owner statement filed with the RCS must be updated within 30 days of any transfer or alteration of effective ownership. During the annual RCS confirmation, the legal representative certifies that the UBO statement remains accurate and that all share transfers have been recorded in the securities movement register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des décisions et procès-verbaux d'assemblées (shareholder decision minute book and AGM record)
Registre des titres de capital et mouvements de titres (securities and share transfer register for registered securities)
Feuilles de présence des assemblées générales (annual general meeting attendance sheets)
Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (beneficial ownership record supporting the RCS UBO declaration)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax on all French-resident companies from fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on up to €42,000 of taxable profit for small companies with net turnover below €10,000,000 and eligible independent ownership. No sector-specific dredging tax holiday exists; general incentives available: Research Tax Credit (CIR) 30% on eligible R&D expenses up to €100,000,000 and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) 20% up to €400,000; reduced 10% effective rate on patent/licence royalty income under Article 39 terdecies CGI.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (liasse fiscale) together with annexes 2050-SD through 2059-SD; mandatory electronic filing via DGFiP 'TéléIR' EFI/EDI portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly corporate income tax instalments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December with final balance at filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months of fiscal year-end; a 31 December year-end uses the statutory 3 May deadline or the next working day when 1 May falls on a weekend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: SIREN/SIRET, legal form, tax regime, registered office, place of effective management, foreign permanent establishments and group relations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned SARL must identify the ultimate beneficial owner and disclose any foreign permanent establishment; filing as a French resident entity is required only if management and control remain in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss from the French statutory financial statements before corporate tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter French statutory results only; attributable profits of a foreign permanent establishment are excluded and reported through treaty relief schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2058-A, 'Résultat fiscal avant imputation des déficits'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result after adding back non-deductible expenses and applying exempt income adjustments, before loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transfer-pricing excessive payments and abusive deductions must be reintegrated; non-resident shareholders cannot use the French SARL structure to strips taxable profit without economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carried-forward tax losses limited to €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income above that threshold in any single year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the proven French entity losses only; carryforward is not available to foreign shareholders or offshore predecessors in the absence of continuity of business and commercial substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty equal to 10% of the assessed tax, rising to 40% after a 30-day formal notice; late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; serious inaccuracy penalty of 40%; intentional fraud or abuse of law penalty of 80% and potential criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% for non-resident individual recipients; 30% for non-resident corporate shareholders; 75% if the beneficiary is established in a non-cooperative State. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may provide a 0% rate for an EU parent holding at least 25% of the capital for 24 months, and most French DTAs reduce the source-state rate to 0%, 5%, 10% or 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before distribution, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide a valid residence certificate and Form 5000 to the paying French SARL and, where required, to DGFiP. The paying company then applies the treaty or Directive rate at source. If excess withholding has occurred, the recipient must file a refund claim with DGFiP within two years of collection, attaching the residence certificate, Form 5000, ownership timeline and beneficial-owner declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents carry a statutory 33.33% withholding tax under Article 182 B, but the EU Interest and Royalties Directive grants a 0% rate for associated EU companies; treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 10%. Interest on at-arm's-length bank debt is generally exempt from French withholding tax in a cross-border context; related-party interest that is excessive or not beneficially owned may be recharacterised as dividends and taxed at 12.8%, 30% or 75%, plus thin-capitalisation restrictions under Article 212 CGI.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000: mandatory Local File and Master File preparation for a French group entity when the French entity or the group to which it belongs has annual net turnover or balance-sheet total above €400,000,000 and is at least 50% controlled by or exercises control over a non-French related party.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies the OECD-aligned substance doctrine through the abuse-of-rights rule under Article L.64 of the French Tax Procedure Code, ATAD CFC rules, the Principal Purpose Test under DTAs and the MLI. For an ISIC 4290 maritime dredging SARL, economic substance must be evidenced by a real French head office, locally employed administrative and marine engineering personnel, dredging vessels and equipment owned or chartered by the French company, project procurement decisions executed from France, and bank accounts held in the French entity's name.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent income-tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of milestone revenues from public port dredging contracts, false subcontractor invoices, unreported offshore accounts, or omission of Form 2065-SD filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 40% or 80% of evaded tax plus late-payment interest; criminal conviction under Article 1741 CGI may result in up to five years imprisonment and a fine of €75,000, together with confiscation of vessels and equipment and prohibition from managing commercial companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who organise or endorse false filings may be jointly and severally liable for tax, penalties and interest. Criminal courts may order imprisonment, travel bans, asset freezing, disqualification from corporate management and mandatory restitution to the French State.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing mispricing and artificial intercompany arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Shifting EPC dredging margin through inflated offshore vessel charter fees, fictitious management charges or low-interest shareholder loans without actual service provision, vessels or documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGFiP recharacterisation to arm's length, additional taxable income, 2.4% annual late-payment interest and a 40% penalty for inadequate documentation. In fraudulent cases the penalty increases to 80% and the file may be referred to the national anti-fraud committee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors who knowingly sign sham transfer-pricing documentation can be held personally liable for the reassessed deficits and penalties, and may face criminal liability for abuse of law or fraudulent misrepresentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the French SARL as a mailbox entity with no local dredging capacity, no operational management, no French bank activity and no economic risk, used solely to route profits to treaty-shopping shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of France's specific anti-abuse rule and the MLI Principal Purpose Test may deny treaty benefits, reclassify the entity as non-resident, impose 80% penalty and disallow carryforward losses. The tax authority may also disregard the legal entity and reassess the actual foreign beneficiary directly, with fines and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners and shadow directors can be pursued personally under the abuse-of-rights doctrine. If the corporate veil is pierced, personal assets may be seized and directors may be subject to travel bans, reputational sanctions and criminal prosecution for organised tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML violations and corruption in public procurement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving public port-authority payments in offshore transit accounts, paying undisclosed commissions in connection with dredging contract awards, or layering milestone proceeds through legal entities to conceal ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering and corruption offences carry imprisonment of up to ten years and fines up to €1,000,000 for natural persons; a SARL can be fined up to €5,000,000 and face the confiscation of corporate vessels, equipment, bank balances and contract rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be imprisoned, prohibited from managing commercial companies, subjected to travel restrictions and ordered to pay restitution to the injured public authority. Criminal forfeiture extends to personal assets where the court determines personal benefit from laundered public funds.
